newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to down, pressured by crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to down, pressured by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to lower again Friday in moderate trade, with sentiment still bearish on weaker crude and sluggish utility demand, industry sources said.

"High sulphur is still pretty weak. People are looking at the Merc (NYMEX) and getting more bearish, but resid is now competitive with (natural) gas and some utilities are switching back to oil," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $19.50-75 a barrel, helped by reports of growing utility interest after recent strength in natgas.
NYH November one percent paper was little changed from late Thursday quotes at $19.25-50, with December paper also steady at $19.55-70. January was pegged at $20.15-35.
High sulphurs in NYH stabilized after Thursday's steep slide, with 2.2 percent still talked at $18.50-75.
U.S. Gulf one percent was off slightly at about $18.25, while three percent tumbled 50 cents to $16.50-75 on reports that 50,000 barrels for prompt delivery sold at $16.50.

New York City gate baseload gas sold Friday in the $3.40/mmBtu area versus NYH November one percent paper at a $3.08/mmBtu equivalent. December gas in New York was quoted at $1.20 over the screen, or about $3.85-3.90/mmBtu, compared to NYH December one percent paper at a $3.12 equivalent.
